acceptance_criteria.notes: Recomputed the design's trust table by hand against traitDelta (diplomat +1/-1/-6, engineer +2/-2/-8, skeptic +1/-4/-10, A100 -4, A0 -12, denied relief): all match and codec_test asserts them. Hold score, stress 5+N/10, regard -(N/10+2) and +1, and the policy strain shift (shift x N/100) match the design; strain_test checks exact numbers. crew-core 121 passed/0 failed/60 skipped on interpreter and --bytecode --strict-bytecode; social-dynamics 166 passed, 0 failed. Old scenarios: no events means no regard relationships and no extra indicator, so the config is unchanged. Re-ran --check seeds 1..20 with the pack policy: ergosphere 9/12, processing-cascade 9/10, news-decades-late 6/6, as REVIEW.md says. Deductions: (a) tie-break is the opposite reading of the design (see defect 1); (b) two negative transfers on one resource under-halt (defect 2); (c) the headline feature fires in 1 of 20 ergosphere runs, so the argument is effectively unexercised outside unit tests; (d) crew-lab make targets and make replay not run (validate in progress).

correctness_robustness.notes: Logic is clean for the single-transfer, single-participant case. Weaknesses are cumulative-loss handling, an unmatched tie-break, and trust numbers that change for existing orders recordings. hearAll now uses an index, so the previous hear-id length defect is fixed (max 76 chars); sf-<32>-<n> is short. Reservation of ev-/yd-/sf-/hear-/ship- prefixes also closes the earlier namespace finding. halt errors propagate as DomainFailure (no swallowing). Yields are unaffected (halted task is Stopped, yields only for Completed).

test_quality.notes: strain_test has 4 exact-number tests (yield order, halted holder regard, both halted, no argument with free units); codec_test covers the table and round trip; policy strain tests cover on/off, N scaling, validation. Missing: tie-break test, two-transfer event, one worker holding two tasks, overextended +15 in the hold score, a strained stance (score >= 100 yields), halt under Pending continuation, and a golden showing CompliedStart changes orders trust vs 0.1.0.

docs_bookkeeping.notes: REVIEW.md is candid: 44/50, arguments 1/20, two failing claims named, navigator-holds-the-heat called vacuous, wrong earlier explanation corrected; I verified these numbers. Claims are not tuned to pass (new failing ones were left failing). Deductions: REVIEW does not name heat-blocks-work-under-orders as still failing in the update (it is the earlier finding 1, still true); CHANGELOG does not warn that orders-policy trust deltas for existing scenarios/recordings now differ from 0.1.0 (CompliedStart/traitDelta and RefusedOrder -4..-12); the sprint JSON status is still in_progress, S5 pending (expected before landing); the knowledge-limit comment in session.ail:~398 was not updated for sf- rows (up to 8 transfers x 32 events x crew).

defects.issue: Tie-break is opposite to the design text. Design: 'ties go to whoever started earlier' (halted first). Code sorts later start first (a.task.started > b.task.started -> -1); the sprint JSON and comment say 'later starts first'. No test covers ties. Either is defensible, but it silently departs from the approved design.
defects.suggestion: Decide and align: change the comparator or amend the design/CHANGELOG, and add a tie test.

defects.issue: argueOne computes the gap per transfer from the pre-event available count, but the transfers are applied afterwards in flow(). An event with two negative transfers on the same resource (e.g. -1 and -1, holders reserving 1 each, 0 available) halts one holder; the second gap then reads available=1 (just released) and is 0, so nobody else is halted, and the second transfer is then capped to 0 applied. The crew lose less than the event says, and only one argument evidence fires. Not tested.
defects.suggestion: Sum negative deltas per resource before arguing (or apply transfer i before computing gap i+1), and add a test.

defects.issue: Behaviour change for existing scenarios and recordings: any orders-policy start now yields CompliedStart (2 - voice) and an overridden refusal yields -4..-12 instead of -8 for actors with OCEAN traits. The 'old scenarios byte-identical' property holds for config/state only for scenarios without events; trust values in orders runs (e.g. recordings/refused-order.ndjson) differ from 0.1.0. make replay compares two runs of the same build, so it cannot detect this.
defects.suggestion: State it in the CHANGELOG and regenerate or assert the affected recordings; consider a version note that trust numbers are not backward compatible.

defects.issue: A worker holding two tasks: both can be in 'halted' or one in halted and one in 'kept'. Stress is applied once per halted task (double stress) and the 'kept' list can contain the halted worker themselves (harmless since regard to self does not exist). Holders are keyed on head(t.participants) only, so multi-participant tasks only argue for the first participant. Scenarios create single-participant work, so unreachable today.
defects.suggestion: Key stances and consequences by worker, or document the single-participant assumption.

defects.issue: Knowledge bound comment says 32 events x 15 crew = 480 rows; each sf- argument adds up to 8 more concerns x crew per event, so the worst case is higher (about 4,300 rows, still under 8,192 but the comment and decode are not updated, and there is no limit test).
defects.suggestion: Update the comment and add a decode-time check or test.

defects.issue: navigator-holds-the-heat (median halted <= 0) passes vacuously whenever nobody is halted (19 of 20 runs). REVIEW.md discloses it, but it counts in the 44/50 headline.
defects.suggestion: Add a 'when shortfalls >= 1' guard, as approach-forces-an-argument has, or report it as untested.

defects.issue: overextended_turns uses the first rule's threshold (head(sim.scenario.rules)); correct today because the scenario gives every worker the same strain block, but it silently breaks if per-worker thresholds are added. regard_min defaults to 100 when a crew member holds no regard (scenarios without events), so a claim of the form regard_min >= x passes trivially there.
defects.suggestion: Look up the threshold per worker (rule overextended_<w>) and document the default.

defects.issue: Does not list heat-blocks-work-under-orders among the failing ergosphere claims although it still fails (stockouts 0); the three failures are approach-forces-an-argument, halted-engineer-resents-navigator and that earlier one.
defects.suggestion: Name it as the carried-over finding 1.

summary: PASS, 80/100. The package changes match the approved formulas and the trust table recomputes exactly; both engines pass; reporting is honest. Risks: tie-break direction differs from the design, multiple negative transfers on one resource under-halt, orders-policy trust numbers change for existing scenarios, and the argument almost never fires in the one scenario built to show it.
